findings.title: Portfolio drift exceeds tolerance in US equity and Canadian bonds
findings.detail: The portfolio is overweight in US equity by {{m:drift.US_EQUITY.pp}} and underweight in Canadian bonds by {{m:drift.CA_BONDS.pp}}. These deviations exceed the tolerance of {{m:cfg.drift_tolerance.pp}}, requiring rebalancing to align with the balanced risk profile.

findings.title: Excess cash in non-registered account awaiting investment
findings.detail: Cash in the non-registered account is {{m:drift.CASH.pp}} above the target of {{m:target.CASH.pct}}. This is consistent with the note regarding the uninvested bonus. Deploying this cash can help address the underweight position in Canadian bonds.

findings.title: Current balanced strategy supports retirement objectives
findings.detail: The model portfolio's expected return of {{m:goal.model_return.pct}} is sufficient to meet the {{m:goal.G1.required.pct}} return required for the client's retirement goal, supporting the current balanced strategy despite the potential for earlier retirement.

The portfolio's current volatility of {{m:risk.vol.pct}} is within the {{m:risk.vol_band_max.pct}} limit for a balanced profile. The portfolio is slightly more volatile than the model portfolio of {{m:risk.target_vol.pct}}, but remains suitable for the client's age and long time horizon.
findings.title: Portfolio volatility is within suitability limits

findings.detail: In an equity bear market scenario, the portfolio would experience a loss of {{m:stress.equity_bear.cad}}, representing a {{m:stress.equity_bear.pct}} decline. Given the client's long time horizon of twenty years and low liquidity needs, this downside is acceptable.
findings.title: Stress test indicates manageable downside risk
No single-security concentration issues identified
findings.detail: No single security exceeds the concentration limit of {{m:conc.limit.pct}}. The portfolio is well-diversified across asset classes, which supports the balanced risk profile.

US equity markets experienced significant growth, with the index returning {{m:mkt.us_equity_ytd.pct}} percent year to date, driven by strong performance in technology sectors. This upward movement likely contributed to an overweight position in the client's US equity holdings.
findings.title: US equity growth drives portfolio drift
Canadian bond yield environment impacts fixed income allocation
findings.detail: Canadian bond yields have trended lower, with the ten-year yield currently at {{m:mkt.ca_10y_yield.pct}} percent. This environment, coupled with a modest year-to-date return of {{m:mkt.ca_bond_ytd.pct}} percent for the Canadian bond index, has influenced the valuation and relative weight of the fixed income portion of the portfolio.

The client holds {{m:tax.l1.VTI.cad}} of VTI in their TFSA. US-listed foreign-dividend funds in a TFSA are subject to a withholding tax on dividends that cannot be recovered. Moving these to an RRSP may be more tax-efficient for long-term growth.
findings.title: US-listed fund held in TFSA

findings.detail: The client has {{m:tax.nonreg_interest.cad}} in interest-bearing assets (CSAV) within their non-registered account. Interest income is fully taxable at the client's marginal rate. Moving these to a tax-advantaged account can improve after-tax returns.
findings.title: Interest-bearing assets in non-registered account

findings.detail: The client has {{m:tax.tfsa_room.cad}} of unused TFSA room while holding {{m:tax.nonreg_interest.cad}} in interest-generating assets in a non-registered account. Utilizing available TFSA room for these assets can shelter the interest income from annual taxation.
findings.title: Unused TFSA room available for taxable interest holdings
